checkpoints.title: Tradeoff duel
checkpoints.prompt: A stream with 2M viewers. How do comments reach them?

options.label: Clients poll every second
options.verdict: 2M viewers polling once a second is 2M requests/sec for a stream that may get ten comments in that time. You have converted a broadcast problem into a request-per-viewer problem.

options.label: Server-sent events over a fanout tier
options.verdict: Comments are one-way from server to client, which is exactly what SSE is for — cheaper than WebSockets and it reconnects on its own. Cost then tracks comment volume rather than viewer count.

defend.prompt: What does a mega-stream still force you to do?

options.label: Batch comments into periodic frames rather than sending each one
Introduce broadcast or relay nodes between publisher and viewers
Sample or rate-limit what is displayed
Guarantee every viewer sees every comment

defend.explain: Nobody can read 500 comments a second, so delivering all of them is neither possible nor useful. You batch, relay through intermediate nodes so no single server fans out to millions, and accept sampling on the largest streams.

checkpoints.title: Capacity ladder
checkpoints.prompt: Comment delivery under roughly 200ms end to end.

rungs.q: Latency target that still feels live
rungs.note: About the human threshold for interaction feeling immediate.

rungs.q: Cost driver with a push transport
rungs.note: Which is the entire reason to push rather than poll.
M broadcast nodes instead of N viewer connections on one box.

checkpoints.explain: Push makes cost proportional to content rather than audience — then hierarchy keeps the fan-out per node bounded.

checkpoints.title: Architecture builder
checkpoints.explain: The comment is persisted and published once; broadcast nodes sit between pub/sub and the socket gateways so no single node fans out to millions. Viewers hold an SSE connection to a gateway. The store is written on the way in, not read on the way out.

checkpoints.title: Spot the bottleneck
checkpoints.prompt: Comments are live on small streams and 90 seconds behind on the biggest one.
checkpoints.explain: Only the largest stream is affected, so this is fan-out per node rather than anything shared. One broadcast node is pushing to 900k connections and cannot keep up — the tier has not scaled with the audience. Add relay depth so each node fans out to a bounded number, and batch comments into frames instead of sending them individually.

wrong.Pub/Sub: 3ms publish — the message is distributed instantly. Delivery to viewers is the problem.
wrong.SSE Gateway: Healthy, and it can only forward what the broadcast tier hands it.
wrong.Comment Service: Ingest is fine; small streams prove the write path works.
